title: Gemma, DeepMind's Family of Open Models — Omar Sanseviero, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Omar Sanseviero presents Gemma 4, Google DeepMind's Apache-2.0 open model family spanning 2B–32B parameters, including on-device E2B/E4B models with per-layer embeddings, a fast MoE, and a 31B dense model. The talk is mostly ecosystem and capability marketing, but a few concrete deployment mechanisms (small local models, CPU/disk offload, fine-tuned task-specific variants) are transferable.

takeaways.technique: Small local model tier for cheap/offline subtasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Gemma 4 ships 2B–4B models that run on phones/laptops and handle coding, agentic skills, and multimodal tasks offline via llama.cpp.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the smallest two models can run in an Android phone, in an iOS, in an iPhone phone as well, even in a Raspberry Pi
takeaways.numbers: 2B–4B params; ~100 tokens/sec on a laptop with 10 parallel instances

takeaways.what_they_do: E2B/E4B use per-layer embeddings as a lookup table that can live in CPU or disk, so only ~2B params need GPU memory; enabled with a llama.cpp flag.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you actually just load 2 billion parameters into the GPU and then the rest can be like much slower memory

takeaways.what_they_do: Google ships narrow variants like Shield Gemma (safety classifiers) and Med-Gemini, showing small fine-tuned models can do one classification job reliably in production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Shield Gemma, which is a family of world rate models. Those are great for production use cases

takeaways.technique: Apache-2.0 self-hosted model as quota fallback
takeaways.what_they_do: Gemma 4 moved to Apache 2.0, removing license friction for self-hosting and fine-tuning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with Gemma 4 we changed our license to an actual Apache 2 license
